pages.text: "These... keep sliding." Nils the little bear stood stiffly on two long wooden skis. Whenever they moved, his legs trembled. His blue boots were fastened firmly to the skis.
"I want to glide all the way down there too." But Nils kept his legs straight as sticks. Then he stayed completely still.
Grandpa Bruno waved a paw at the bottom of the slope. Nils could not lift a foot and stayed where he was. "What if I fall?" His knees grew even stiffer.
Then one ski slipped a little forward. Nils fell backward with a thump! Snow slipped down the back of his neck, making him shiver.
Grandpa walked up the slope and stood beside him. "We do not have to start at the top today. Let us begin on this low part." He held his broad palm out to Nils.
Nils clasped that palm with his paw. "Now bend your knees a little. Bend your knees and glide!" As Nils bent them slightly, he slid gently forward.
"Oh? I did not fall!" His mouth opened wide. Holding Grandpa's paw, he went one step, then two more down the slope. The two skis slipped through the snow side by side.
"This time I will try alone." Nils gently let go. He bent his knees and relaxed his shoulders. Glide—he slid to the bottom of the low slope.
Nils waddled back up. "One, start low! Two, bend your knees a little! Three, relax your shoulders!" He glided down alone again. "Bend your knees and glide!"
Snug in Grandpa's arms, Nils raised both paws above his head. Even something scary becomes possible when you start low. "Tomorrow I will start up there! Bend your knees and glide!"
